transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep losing important papers and tools I need for jobs, and it’s starting to hurt my business. It has gotten to a point where I just can't keep track of things anymore, and I really need some help figuring out what to do.
Have you noticed any difficulties with memory, such as forgetting appointments, conversations, or tasks you need to complete, in addition to losing physical items?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. When clients are explaining what they want, my mind often drifts off and I have to ask them to repeat themselves. I also frequently miss deadlines, double-book jobs, and leave paperwork half-finished because I get overwhelmed trying to manage it all.
Do you find it hard to focus or pay attention to details, or do you make careless mistakes in your work or daily activities, aside from just losing things or forgetting appointments?

Yes, I definitely make careless mistakes with details. When I'm writing up bids or ordering materials, I'll think I've checked everything, but then I'll realize later I misread a measurement or left off a cabinet door. It's really embarrassing having to call the customer back to fix what should've been a simple detail.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have an inability to stay seated, especially in quiet environments, or do you feel like you're always 'on the go'?

Yes, I definitely feel a restless buzz inside whenever I have to sit still, like during a client meeting or waiting at the bank, so I'll start tapping my foot or shifting around. Even trying to relax quietly on the porch makes me get so fidgety and antsy that I have to start fiddling with something just to keep busy.
Have you experienced any significant emotional difficulties, such as persistent feelings of anxiety, depression, or irritability, that seem to be impacting your daily life and interactions?

I do feel a lot of anxiety and worry about whether I can keep my carpentry business stable enough to someday open the women's mentoring workshop I've dreamed of. But while I'm highly stressed and anxious about these business setbacks, I don't experience persistent depression or irritability.
Have you experienced these symptoms of inattention, restlessness, and disorganization throughout your life, or did they start more recently, perhaps in response to the stress of your business?

While these issues became completely unmanageable about a year ago when I took over the business administration, I've actually struggled with them my whole life. Even back in elementary school, I was always losing permission slips, forgetting homework, and daydreaming. My teachers used to tell my parents that I was smart but just couldn't stay focused or organized.

You mentioned that these issues have been present your whole life, but they became particularly unmanageable about a year ago with the added stress of your business. Can you tell me more about how these symptoms affected your life during childhood and adolescence, before you took over the business?

Back in school, I was always the kid who forgot to bring homework home and constantly lost permission slips. I spent a lot of time daydreaming through instructions instead of listening to the teacher. They always told my parents that I was smart, but that I just couldn't seem to pay attention or stay organized.
Did you often interrupt others, blurt out answers, or have difficulty waiting for your turn when you were a child or teenager?
I don't really recall having those specific problems with interrupting or waiting my turn as a kid. Back then, I was mostly just daydreamy, forgetful, and disorganized.
Did you ever feel like you were constantly on the move, had trouble engaging in quiet leisure activities, or felt an internal restlessness during your childhood and adolescence?

No, I don't recall feeling particularly restless, hyperactive, or "on the move" during my childhood or adolescence. Back then, my struggles were more about daydreaming, forgetting to bring homework home, and losing permission slips. Teachers would just say I was smart but didn't pay attention or stay organized.

You've mentioned feeling restless and fidgety now, but not as much during childhood and adolescence. Can you think of any specific situations or activities as a child where you might have exhibited excessive running, climbing, or other hyperactive behaviors that got you into trouble or stood out to your parents or teachers?

No, I don't recall having those kinds of physically hyperactive behaviors like excessive running or climbing as a child. My struggles back then were much more quiet, like daydreaming through instructions, forgetting to bring homework home, and losing permission slips. My teachers always just said I was smart but couldn't stay organized or pay attention.

You've described having symptoms of inattention and disorganization throughout your life, but with restlessness and fidgetiness becoming more noticeable as an adult, especially with the added stress of your business; can you think of any factors or events that might have contributed to the emergence or worsening of these restlessness symptoms in adulthood?

It really became noticeable after my husband passed away a year and a half ago and I had to take over the office work. Before, I was always moving around doing hands-on carpentry, but now I'm forced to sit still for long periods doing billing, waiting at the bank, or in client meetings. That forced stillness triggers this intense internal "restless buzz" where I just have to fidget or tap my feet.

You mentioned that your restlessness and fidgetiness became more noticeable in adulthood, but can you confirm whether you had any symptoms of hyperactivity, such as excessive running, climbing, or restlessness, before the age of 7?

I don't recall having those specific hyperactive symptoms like excessive running or climbing when I was young. But I definitely remember being very daydreamy, forgetful, and disorganized during my elementary school years.

To confirm, you're certain you didn't exhibit any noticeable hyperactive behaviors, such as excessive running, climbing, or an inability to sit still, before the age of 7, which is a key criterion for differentiating between attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and other conditions?

Yes, I'm certain I didn't exhibit those physical hyperactive behaviors like excessive running or climbing as a child. Instead, my struggles in elementary school were focused on inattentiveness and disorganization, like daydreaming, forgetting my homework, and constantly losing permission slips.

Just to clarify, you're absolutely sure you didn't exhibit any hyperactive behaviors, such as excessive running, climbing, or an inability to sit still, before the age of 7, which could help differentiate between possible diagnoses?

Yes, I am completely sure I didn't have those hyperactive behaviors like running around or climbing on things when I was little. My struggles in elementary school were strictly about inattention and disorganization, like daydreaming through instructions, losing permission slips, and forgetting my homework.
Is it possible that you might have exhibited some hyperactive behaviors before the age of 7, but they were not noticed or reported by your parents or teachers, which could impact the diagnosis?

I really don't think so, as I was never a wild, hyperactive, or disruptive kid. My struggles in early elementary school were always about being daydreamy, forgetting my homework, losing permission slips, and being disorganized. My parents and teachers definitely noticed those things, but they just attributed it to me not paying attention.

Are you absolutely certain that you didn't exhibit any signs of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting, restlessness, or an inability to sit still, before the age of 7, even if it was mild or not reported by your parents or teachers?

Yes, I am sure that as far as I can remember, I didn't have those hyperactive or physically restless symptoms as a young child. My struggles in elementary school were much more about daydreaming, forgetting my homework, losing permission slips, and being disorganized. I was never physically unable to sit still back then.

To finalize, you're confirming that you did not exhibit any noticeable symptoms of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting, restlessness, or an inability to sit still, before the age of 7, which is crucial for distinguishing between different diagnoses?

Yes, I can confirm that I didn't have those hyperactive or restless symptoms as a child. Looking back at my elementary school days, my issues were much more about daydreaming, forgetting homework, and being disorganized, rather than being physically fidgety or unable to sit still.

Is there any possibility that you might have had mild symptoms of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting or restlessness, before the age of 7 that were not significant enough to be noticed or reported by your parents or teachers?

I really don't recall having those specific hyperactive, fidgety, or restless symptoms when I was that young. As far as I can remember, my issues back in elementary school were mostly related to daydreaming, forgetting things, and being disorganized, rather than being physically hyperactive.

Can you think of any situation or event from your childhood, no matter how minor, where you might have exhibited hyperactive behavior, such as excessive fidgeting or restlessness, that could have been overlooked or not reported?

I really don't recall any times where I was physically hyperactive, fidgety, or restless as a child. Instead, my struggles back then were strictly about daydreaming, forgetting to bring homework home, losing permission slips, and being disorganized, which my teachers often commented on.

Is it possible that your parents or teachers might have overlooked or not reported any symptoms of hyperactivity in you before the age of 7, or are you certain that such behaviors were completely absent?

I'm not sure if hyperactivity was overlooked, but my parents and teachers never mentioned me being physically hyperactive or disruptive. The feedback I did get was entirely about me being daydreamy, disorganized, forgetting homework, and losing permission slips. The focus was really just on my inattentiveness back then.

You've consistently reported not having hyperactive symptoms before the age of 7, but can you think of any reason or circumstance that might have led to the emergence of restlessness and fidgetiness in adulthood, such as a significant life change or stressor, that could help differentiate between possible diagnoses like ADHD and other conditions?

The restless, fidgety feelings became highly noticeable and unmanageable about a year and a half ago after my husband unexpectedly passed away. Taking on all the business administration, billing, and scheduling on top of my physical carpentry work has been an immense stressor, and having to sit still to do paperwork or attend long meetings is when I feel that inner "buzz" and can't stay calm.

To confirm once more, you are certain that you did not exhibit any symptoms of hyperactivity, such as excessive running, climbing, or restlessness, before the age of 7, and these symptoms only became noticeable in adulthood, particularly after taking on more administrative tasks and experiencing significant life stressors?

Yes, that is correct. In elementary school, my struggles were strictly focused on daydreaming, losing homework, and disorganization rather than physical hyperactivity like running or climbing. The restless feelings and the major difficulties managing them only became prominent in adulthood after my husband passed away and I had to take on all the administrative work for the business.

Can you describe how your symptoms of inattention and disorganization have impacted your daily life and relationships over time, and whether you've noticed any patterns or triggers that make them better or worse?

Over the past year, my disorganization has led to late invoices, mixed-up schedules, and frustrated clients, making me worry I won't be able to keep the business stable enough to start my dream women's mentoring workshop. These issues really trigger when I try to handle administrative tasks like billing and contracts, which became unmanageable after my husband passed away, whereas the hands-on carpentry work still comes easily to me.

Can you describe any situations where you feel your restlessness and fidgetiness are most pronounced, and whether these feelings have impacted your ability to perform daily tasks or maintain relationships?

The restlessness is worst when I have to sit still, like during long client meetings or waiting at the bank, where I get this "restless buzz" inside and constantly tap my foot or shift in my chair. Even trying to relax quietly on the porch or read a book doesn't work, because I get so antsy within minutes that I have to start talking to whoever is around or fiddling with a project.
Is it possible that any hyperactive behaviors you might have exhibited before the age of 7 were mild or not noticed by your parents or teachers, which could affect the diagnosis?

I really don't recall having any hyperactive or physically restless behaviors as a young child. However, my inattentive symptoms—like daydreaming, forgetting homework, losing permission slips, and being disorganized—were definitely present in elementary school. My parents and teachers noticed these and often commented that I was smart but struggled to pay attention.

To finalize your diagnosis, can you once again confirm whether you are absolutely certain that you did not exhibit any noticeable symptoms of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting or restlessness, before the age of 7, which is crucial for distinguishing between F90.0 and F98.8?

Yes, I am absolutely sure. Looking back to my childhood and elementary school years, my struggles were strictly with daydreaming, forgetting homework, losing permission slips, and disorganization. I never experienced any physical hyperactivity, fidgeting, or restlessness back then.

Is there anything else you can remember or any family member who might recall if you exhibited any signs of hyperactivity, such as excessive fidgeting or restlessness, before the age of 7 that might have been overlooked?

No, my family and I don't recall me ever being physically hyperactive, wild, or excessively fidgety as a young child. Instead, my struggles in elementary school were always about daydreaming, forgetting to bring homework home, losing permission slips, and being disorganized. Those were the exact things my teachers always pointed out to my parents.

Are you certain that the restlessness and fidgetiness you experience now did not have a mild or subtle onset before the age of 7, but perhaps became more pronounced in adulthood due to significant life changes or stressors?

Yes, I'm quite sure. Looking back at my childhood, the main issues were always daydreaming, forgetting homework, and losing things, rather than any physical restlessness. That "restless buzz" and fidgeting really only started feeling prominent in my adulthood, especially with the stress of losing my husband and trying to run the business alone.

Can you think of any way that your current symptoms of restlessness and fidgetiness might be related to or distinct from the inattentive symptoms you experienced as a child, considering the significant life changes you've undergone?

As a kid, my issues were quiet, like daydreaming and forgetting homework while teachers said I was smart but disorganized. Now, I have this physical, buzzing restlessness where I constantly fidget and tap my feet when trying to sit still. Ever since my husband passed and I've had to force myself to sit down and handle the business paperwork, this need to keep moving has become much more noticeable and frustrating than it ever was when I was younger.

Can you confirm whether the emergence of your restlessness and fidgetiness in adulthood is directly related to the increased stress and life changes, such as taking over the business, or if it might be an independent development of symptoms?

I'm not entirely sure if the restlessness is a direct result of the recent stress and business changes or if it's a separate issue. However, it has definitely become much more noticeable and harder to manage since I had to take over all the administrative tasks for the business.
